_GeneralInformation.ShortName: California RC Bridges 2025 (Chen et al.) - Bridge Components
_GeneralInformation.Description: Component-level seismic fragility models for California reinforced concrete bridges from the database of Chen et al. (2025), Earthquake Spectra 41(4), doi:10.1177/87552930251343634, published on DesignSafe as PRJ-5910 (doi:10.17603/ds2-c73m-nj37, version 1, Open Data Commons Attribution License). The database compiles fragility curves from published studies and assigns them to 26 bridge groups. A group code gives the design era (E1 pre-1970, E2 1971–1990, E3 post-1991, E123 any era), the number of spans (S1 one, S2 two, S3P three or more), the bent type (C0 no bents, C1 single-column bents, C2P multi-column bents), and the abutment type (D diaphragm, S seat). Model IDs follow the pattern CRCB.<era>.<spans>.<bents>.<abutment>.<component>.<attributes>.<source>, where the attributes describe the deck, the bent configuration (two-column, or three to five columns), the modeled span count, frames, in-span hinges, column shape, direction, modification basis, abutment foundation, and approach slab, and the last segment names the source study. Each curve gives the probability of reaching or exceeding a damage state as a function of Sa(1.0 s), the spectral acceleration at a period of 1.0 s, in g. The component fragilities of this dataset and the system fragilities of the dataset of the same name (seismic/transportation_network/portfolio/California RC Bridges 2025) are two representations of the same bridge. Apply one or the other to a given bridge, because applying both to the same bridge double-counts its damage; different bridges in one regional assessment may use different representations. Curves for the same component within a group come from different studies and are alternatives; the database publishes no weights for choosing among them. The Cavalcante et al. (2022) curves in the E123 groups (single-span bridges) are, or are derived from, curves for Brazilian bridges, which Chen et al. (2025) use as a proxy for California single-span bridges; the approach-settlement curves of Shao et al. (2022) in those groups are for California bridges. Chen et al. (2025) found no era-specific fragility models for single-span bridges, so the E123 groups apply to bridges of any era. Entries that are N/A in the slight and moderate median and dispersion, the only states their components define, with the extensive and complete cells empty, are omitted: 71 column foundation rotation (FndRot) entries, all those in the 24 groups where the component occurs except 1 of the 4 in E1-S2-C2P-S; 24 shear key (Key) entries, all those in E2-S2-C1-S, E2-S2-C2P-S, E2-S3P-C1-S, E2-S3P-C2P-S, E3-S2-C1-S, E3-S2-C2P-S, E3-S3P-C1-S, and E3-S3P-C2P-S. The database uses N/A to mark a negligible probability of damage from ground shaking. The Comments of each model record the source study, its ground-motion suite, and every correction or inherited value.

CRCB.E1.S2.C1.D.AbAct.BoxGirder.Circ.M17.Description: Active abutment fragility for an Era 1 (pre-1970) bridge with two spans, single-column bents, and diaphragm abutments. Model attributes: box-girder deck, circular columns.
CRCB.E1.S2.C1.D.AbAct.BoxGirder.Circ.M17.Comments:
DesignSafe PRJ-5910 v1, Sa_1_Fragility Database.csv, data row 56 (spreadsheet row 58), group E1-S2-C1-D, AbAct; source note "Box-girder, circular column". The curve describes the most-damaged unit of this component type in the bridge (the source analyses record one peak demand per component type), so assign a quantity of one per bridge. Curves for the same component and group from different sources are alternatives, and the database publishes no weights for choosing among them. The component curves do not carry the demand correlation behind the system curves. The component curves and the system curve of the same group (seismic/transportation_network/portfolio/California RC Bridges 2025) are two representations of the same bridge. Apply one or the other to a given bridge, because applying both to the same bridge double-counts its damage; different bridges in one regional assessment may use different representations.

Source study: Mangalathu (2017), a doctoral thesis that groups California box-girder bridges into classes by design era, span count, bent type, abutment type, and column shape, and derives component and system fragilities for each class from nonlinear time-history analyses. The fragility analyses use 320 scaled motions from 228 records of a Caltrans NGA-West2 suite listed in thesis Appendix A. Sa(1.0 s) is the RotD50 spectral acceleration at 5% damping: for 317 of the 320 motions, the Appendix A value equals the NGA-West2 RotD50 value times the tabulated scale factor.

DS1.Description: Slight damage: aesthetic or minor functional damage to the abutment in the active direction, near first yield of the abutment piles; active abutment displacement exceeds a median capacity of 1.5 in.

DS2.Description: Moderate damage: major functional damage to the abutment in the active direction, near the ultimate deformation of the abutment piles; active abutment displacement exceeds a median capacity of 4 in.

Source study: Shao, Xie, Roblee, and Zhang (2022), a study of approach backfill differential settlement for California bridges. The integrated fragility model of the study takes the mean of the three methods' medians and the square root of the sum of squares (SRSS) of their dispersions. The 2D dynamic method uses 320 motions from a parallel Caltrans project with scale factors of 0.8 to 2.5, whose count and range agree with the Caltrans suite of Mangalathu (2017); the 1D static method works from PGA and the 1D dynamic method from stochastic motions, so neither uses these records. The slight and moderate states are the Minor (LS2) and Moderate (LS3) states of the study; its Observable, Major, and Severe states are not included. In the study, the 10 ft approach slab represents early-designed bridges. It distinguishes abutment foundation types, not seat and diaphragm abutments, so the same curves appear in seat and diaphragm groups. The horizontal-component definition and the spectral damping of Sa(1.0 s) are not stated.

DS1.Description: Slight damage, the Minor (LS2) state of Shao et al. (2022): rotation of the 10 ft approach slab from backfill settlement, with a slope change of about 1/80 to 1/40; approach settlement exceeds a median capacity of 2.1 in.

DS2.Description: Moderate damage, the Moderate (LS3) state of Shao et al. (2022): rotation of the 10 ft approach slab from backfill settlement, with a slope change of about 1/40 to 1/20; approach settlement exceeds a median capacity of 4.2 in.

CRCB.E1.S2.C2P.D.AbPass.BoxGirder.TCB.Ci.Description: Passive abutment fragility for an Era 1 (pre-1970) bridge with two spans, multi-column bents, and diaphragm abutments. Model attributes: box-girder deck, two-column bents, circular columns.
CRCB.E1.S2.C2P.D.AbPass.BoxGirder.TCB.Ci.Comments:
DesignSafe PRJ-5910 v1, Sa_1_Fragility Database.csv, data row 78 (spreadsheet row 80), group E1-S2-C2P-D, AbPass; source note "Box-girder, circular column". The curve describes the most-damaged unit of this component type in the bridge (the source analyses record one peak demand per component type), so assign a quantity of one per bridge. Curves for the same component and group from different sources are alternatives, and the database publishes no weights for choosing among them. The component curves do not carry the demand correlation behind the system curves. The component curves and the system curve of the same group (seismic/transportation_network/portfolio/California RC Bridges 2025) are two representations of the same bridge. Apply one or the other to a given bridge, because applying both to the same bridge double-counts its damage; different bridges in one regional assessment may use different representations.

Source study: Mangalathu (2017), a doctoral thesis that groups California box-girder bridges into classes by design era, span count, bent type, abutment type, and column shape, and derives component and system fragilities for each class from nonlinear time-history analyses. Source study: Shao, Xie, Roblee, and Zhang (2022), a study of approach backfill differential settlement for California bridges. The integrated fragility model of the study takes the mean of the three methods' medians and the square root of the sum of squares (SRSS) of their dispersions. The 2D dynamic method uses 320 motions from a parallel Caltrans project with scale factors of 0.8 to 2.5, whose count and range agree with the Caltrans suite of Mangalathu (2017); the 1D static method works from PGA and the 1D dynamic method from stochastic motions, so neither uses these records. The slight and moderate states are the Minor (LS2) and Moderate (LS3) states of the study; its Observable, Major, and Severe states are not included. In the study, the 10 ft approach slab represents early-designed bridges. It distinguishes abutment foundation types, not seat and diaphragm abutments, so the same curves appear in seat and diaphragm groups. The horizontal-component definition and the spectral damping of Sa(1.0 s) are not stated.

DS1.Description: Slight damage, the Minor (LS2) state of Shao et al. (2022): rotation of the 10 ft approach slab from backfill settlement, with a slope change of about 1/80 to 1/40; approach settlement exceeds a median capacity of 2.1 in.

DS2.Description: Moderate damage, the Moderate (LS3) state of Shao et al. (2022): rotation of the 10 ft approach slab from backfill settlement, with a slope change of about 1/40 to 1/20; approach settlement exceeds a median capacity of 4.2 in.

The curve describes the most-damaged unit of this component type in the bridge (the source analyses record one peak demand per component type), so assign a quantity of one per bridge. Curves for the same component and group from different sources are alternatives, and the database publishes no weights for choosing among them. The component curves do not carry the demand correlation behind the system curves. The component curves and the system curve of the same group (seismic/transportation_network/portfolio/California RC Bridges 2025) are two representations of the same bridge. Apply one or the other to a given bridge, because applying both to the same bridge double-counts its damage; different bridges in one regional assessment may use different representations.

Source study: Mangalathu (2017), a doctoral thesis that groups California box-girder bridges into classes by design era, span count, bent type, abutment type, and column shape, and derives component and system fragilities for each class from nonlinear time-history analyses. The fragility analyses use 320 scaled motions from 228 records of a Caltrans NGA-West2 suite listed in thesis Appendix A. Sa(1.0 s) is the RotD50 spectral acceleration at 5% damping: for 317 of the 320 motions, the Appendix A value equals the NGA-West2 RotD50 value times the tabulated scale factor.

DS1.Description: Slight damage: aesthetic or minor functional damage to the abutment in the active direction, near first yield of the abutment piles; active abutment displacement exceeds a median capacity of 1.5 in.

DS2.Description: Moderate damage: major functional damage to the abutment in the active direction, near the ultimate deformation of the abutment piles; active abutment displacement exceeds a median capacity of 4 in.

CRCB.E1.S2.C2P.S.Approach.Cant.Slope10.S.Comments:
DesignSafe PRJ-5910 v1, Sa_1_Fragility Database.csv, data row 521 (spreadsheet row 523), group E1-S2-C2P-S, Approach; source note "Cantilever abutment on spread footing with approach slab (length 10 ft) damage through slope offset". The curve describes the most-damaged unit of this component type in the bridge (the source analyses record one peak demand per component type), so assign a quantity of one per bridge. Curves for the same component and group from different sources are alternatives, and the database publishes no weights for choosing among them. The component curves do not carry the demand correlation behind the system curves. The component curves and the system curve of the same group (seismic/transportation_network/portfolio/California RC Bridges 2025) are two representations of the same bridge. Apply one or the other to a given bridge, because applying both to the same bridge double-counts its damage; different bridges in one regional assessment may use different representations.

Source study: Shao, Xie, Roblee, and Zhang (2022), a study of approach backfill differential settlement for California bridges. The integrated fragility model of the study takes the mean of the three methods' medians and the square root of the sum of squares (SRSS) of their dispersions. The 2D dynamic method uses 320 motions from a parallel Caltrans project with scale factors of 0.8 to 2.5, whose count and range agree with the Caltrans suite of Mangalathu (2017); the 1D static method works from PGA and the 1D dynamic method from stochastic motions, so neither uses these records. The slight and moderate states are the Minor (LS2) and Moderate (LS3) states of the study; its Observable, Major, and Severe states are not included. In the study, the 10 ft approach slab represents early-designed bridges. It distinguishes abutment foundation types, not seat and diaphragm abutments, so the same curves appear in seat and diaphragm groups. The horizontal-component definition and the spectral damping of Sa(1.0 s) are not stated.

DS1.Description: Slight damage, the Minor (LS2) state of Shao et al. (2022): rotation of the 10 ft approach slab from backfill settlement, with a slope change of about 1/80 to 1/40; approach settlement exceeds a median capacity of 2.1 in.

DS2.Description: Moderate damage, the Moderate (LS3) state of Shao et al. (2022): rotation of the 10 ft approach slab from backfill settlement, with a slope change of about 1/40 to 1/20; approach settlement exceeds a median capacity of 4.2 in.

DS4.Description: Complete damage: loss of seat support, with potential unseating of the span; joint opening exceeds a median capacity of 3 in. (Era 1).

Source study: Shao, Xie, Roblee, and Zhang (2022), a study of approach backfill differential settlement for California bridges. The integrated fragility model of the study takes the mean of the three methods' medians and the square root of the sum of squares (SRSS) of their dispersions. The 2D dynamic method uses 320 motions from a parallel Caltrans project with scale factors of 0.8 to 2.5, whose count and range agree with the Caltrans suite of Mangalathu (2017); the 1D static method works from PGA and the 1D dynamic method from stochastic motions, so neither uses these records. It distinguishes abutment foundation types, not seat and diaphragm abutments, so the same curves appear in seat and diaphragm groups. The horizontal-component definition and the spectral damping of Sa(1.0 s) are not stated.

DesignSafe PRJ-5910 v1, Sa_1_Fragility Database.csv, data row 265 (spreadsheet row 267), group E1-S3P-C2P-D, AbTran; source note "Box-girder, circular column". The curve describes the most-damaged unit of this component type in the bridge (the source analyses record one peak demand per component type), so assign a quantity of one per bridge. Curves for the same component and group from different sources are alternatives, and the database publishes no weights for choosing among them. The component curves do not carry the demand correlation behind the system curves. The component curves and the system curve of the same group (seismic/transportation_network/portfolio/California RC Bridges 2025) are two representations of the same bridge. Apply one or the other to a given bridge, because applying both to the same bridge double-counts its damage; different bridges in one regional assessment may use different representations.

Source study: Mangalathu (2017), a doctoral thesis that groups California box-girder bridges into classes by design era, span count, bent type, abutment type, and column shape, and derives component and system fragilities for each class from nonlinear time-history analyses. The fragility analyses use 320 scaled motions from 228 records of a Caltrans NGA-West2 suite listed in thesis Appendix A. Sa(1.0 s) is the RotD50 spectral acceleration at 5% damping: for 317 of the 320 motions, the Appendix A value equals the NGA-West2 RotD50 value times the tabulated scale factor.

DS1.Description: Slight damage: aesthetic or minor functional damage to the abutment in the transverse direction, near first yield of the abutment piles; transverse abutment displacement exceeds a median capacity of 1 in.

DS2.Description: Moderate damage: major functional damage to the abutment in the transverse direction, near the ultimate deformation of the abutment piles; transverse abutment displacement exceeds a median capacity of 4 in.

DesignSafe PRJ-5910 v1, Sa_1_Fragility Database.csv, data row 285 (spreadsheet row 287), group E1-S3P-C2P-D, Approach; source note "Cantilever abutment on spread footing with approach slab (length 10 ft) damage through slope offset". The curve describes the most-damaged unit of this component type in the bridge (the source analyses record one peak demand per component type), so assign a quantity of one per bridge. Curves for the same component and group from different sources are alternatives, and the database publishes no weights for choosing among them. Source study: Shao, Xie, Roblee, and Zhang (2022), a study of approach backfill differential settlement for California bridges. The integrated fragility model of the study takes the mean of the three methods' medians and the square root of the sum of squares (SRSS) of their dispersions. The 2D dynamic method uses 320 motions from a parallel Caltrans project with scale factors of 0.8 to 2.5, whose count and range agree with the Caltrans suite of Mangalathu (2017); the 1D static method works from PGA and the 1D dynamic method from stochastic motions, so neither uses these records. The slight and moderate states are the Minor (LS2) and Moderate (LS3) states of the study; its Observable, Major, and Severe states are not included. In the study, the 10 ft approach slab represents early-designed bridges. It distinguishes abutment foundation types, not seat and diaphragm abutments, so the same curves appear in seat and diaphragm groups. The horizontal-component definition and the spectral damping of Sa(1.0 s) are not stated.

DS1.Description: Slight damage, the Minor (LS2) state of Shao et al. (2022): rotation of the 10 ft approach slab from backfill settlement, with a slope change of about 1/80 to 1/40; approach settlement exceeds a median capacity of 2.1 in.

DS2.Description: Moderate damage, the Moderate (LS3) state of Shao et al. (2022): rotation of the 10 ft approach slab from backfill settlement, with a slope change of about 1/40 to 1/20; approach settlement exceeds a median capacity of 4.2 in.

DS3.Description: Extensive damage: exposed core and yielding of the transverse reinforcement; major repairs are needed, but the column keeps its function; column curvature ductility exceeds a median capacity of 5 (Era 1).

DS4.Description: Complete damage: longitudinal bar buckling, core crushing, or large drift; the column function is compromised and the column (or the bridge) is replaced; column curvature ductility exceeds a median capacity of 8 (Era 1).

CRCB.E1.S3P.C2P.D.DeckMax.BoxGirder.MCB..Description: Deck displacement fragility for an Era 1 (pre-1970) bridge with three or more spans, multi-column bents, and diaphragm abutments. Model attributes: box-girder deck, bents with three to five columns, circular columns.
CRCB.E1.S3P.C2P.D.DeckMax.BoxGirder.MCB..Comments:
DesignSafe PRJ-5910 v1, Sa_1_Fragility Database.csv, data row 271 (spreadsheet row 273), group E1-S3P-C2P-D, DeckMax; source note "Box-girder, circular column". The curve describes the most-damaged unit of this component type in the bridge (the source analyses record one peak demand per component type), so assign a quantity of one per bridge. Curves for the same component and group from different sources are alternatives, and the database publishes no weights for choosing among them. The component curves do not carry the demand correlation behind the system curves. The component curves and the system curve of the same group (seismic/transportation_network/portfolio/California RC Bridges 2025) are two representations of the same bridge. Apply one or the other to a given bridge, because applying both to the same bridge double-counts its damage; different bridges in one regional assessment may use different representations.

Source study: Mangalathu (2017), a doctoral thesis that groups California box-girder bridges into classes by design era, span count, bent type, abutment type, and column shape, and derives component and system fragilities for each class from nonlinear time-history analyses. The fragility analyses use 320 scaled motions from 228 records of a Caltrans NGA-West2 suite listed in thesis Appendix A. Sa(1.0 s) is the RotD50 spectral acceleration at 5% damping: for 317 of the 320 motions, the Appendix A value equals the NGA-West2 RotD50 value times the tabulated scale factor.

The parameters are identical to those of CRCB.E1.S3P.C2P.D.DeckMax.BoxGirder.MCB.Rect.M17; the duplication is in the source.

Source study: Shao, Xie, Roblee, and Zhang (2022), a study of approach backfill differential settlement for California bridges. The integrated fragility model of the study takes the mean of the three methods' medians and the square root of the sum of squares (SRSS) of their dispersions. The 2D dynamic method uses 320 motions from a parallel Caltrans project with scale factors of 0.8 to 2.5, whose count and range agree with the Caltrans suite of Mangalathu (2017); the 1D static method works from PGA and the 1D dynamic method from stochastic motions, so neither uses these records. The slight and moderate states are the Minor (LS2) and Moderate (LS3) states of the study; its Observable, Major, and Severe states are not included. In the study, the 10 ft approach slab represents early-designed bridges. It distinguishes abutment foundation types, not seat and diaphragm abutments, so the same curves appear in seat and diaphragm groups. The horizontal-component definition and the spectral damping of Sa(1.0 s) are not stated.

The slight and moderate states are the Minor (LS2) and Moderate (LS3) states of the study; its Observable, Major, and Severe states are not included. In the study, the 10 ft approach slab represents early-designed bridges. It distinguishes abutment foundation types, not seat and diaphragm abutments, so the same curves appear in seat and diaphragm groups. The horizontal-component definition and the spectral damping of Sa(1.0 s) are not stated.

DS2.Description: Moderate damage, the Moderate (LS3) state of Shao et al. (2022): step offset between the approach pavement and the abutment from backfill settlement; approach settlement exceeds a median capacity of 2.5 in.

Source study: Shao, Xie, Roblee, and Zhang (2022), a study of approach backfill differential settlement for California bridges. The integrated fragility model of the study takes the mean of the three methods' medians and the square root of the sum of squares (SRSS) of their dispersions. The 2D dynamic method uses 320 motions from a parallel Caltrans project with scale factors of 0.8 to 2.5, whose count and range agree with the Caltrans suite of Mangalathu (2017); the 1D static method works from PGA and the 1D dynamic method from stochastic motions, so neither uses these records. The slight and moderate states are the Minor (LS2) and Moderate (LS3) states of the study; its Observable, Major, and Severe states are not included. In the study, the 10 ft approach slab represents early-designed bridges. It distinguishes abutment foundation types, not seat and diaphragm abutments, so the same curves appear in seat and diaphragm groups. The horizontal-component definition and the spectral damping of Sa(1.0 s) are not stated.

CRCB.E123.S1.C0.S.AbPass.Slab.CPR22.Description: Passive abutment fragility for a single-span (any era) bridge with no bents and seat abutments. Model attributes: slab deck.
CRCB.E123.S1.C0.S.AbPass.Slab.CPR22.Comments:
DesignSafe PRJ-5910 v1, Sa_1_Fragility Database.csv, data row 26 (spreadsheet row 28), group E123-S1-C0-S, AbAct; source note "Slab deck". The curve describes the most-damaged unit of this component type in the bridge (the source analyses record one peak demand per component type), so assign a quantity of one per bridge. Curves for the same component and group from different sources are alternatives, and the database publishes no weights for choosing among them. The component curves do not carry the demand correlation behind the system curves. The component curves and the system curve of the same group (seismic/transportation_network/portfolio/California RC Bridges 2025) are two representations of the same bridge. Apply one or the other to a given bridge, because applying both to the same bridge double-counts its damage; different bridges in one regional assessment may use different representations.

Source study: Cavalcante et al. (2022), a study of typical bridges in northeastern Brazil, including single-span T-beam and slab-deck bridges with seat abutments. Chen et al. (2025) use these curves as a proxy for California single-span bridges. They found no era-specific fragility models for single-span bridges, so the E123 groups apply to bridges of any era. The horizontal-component definition and the spectral damping of Sa(1.0 s) are not stated.

The source lists this curve as AbAct; its values are those that Cavalcante et al. (2022, Table 9) give for the passive abutment, so it is stored as AbPass.

DS1.Description: Slight damage: aesthetic or minor functional damage to the abutment backwall, at about 0.5% drift at the top of the backwall; passive abutment displacement exceeds a median capacity of 3 in.

DS2.Description: Moderate damage: major functional damage to the abutment backwall, which may also require replacing the approach slab; passive abutment displacement exceeds a median capacity of 10 in.

Source study: Shao, Xie, Roblee, and Zhang (2022), a study of approach backfill differential settlement for California bridges. The integrated fragility model of the study takes the mean of the three methods' medians and the square root of the sum of squares (SRSS) of their dispersions. The 2D dynamic method uses 320 motions from a parallel Caltrans project with scale factors of 0.8 to 2.5, whose count and range agree with the Caltrans suite of Mangalathu (2017); the 1D static method works from PGA and the 1D dynamic method from stochastic motions, so neither uses these records. The slight and moderate states are the Minor (LS2) and Moderate (LS3) states of the study; its Observable, Major, and Severe states are not included. In the study, the 10 ft approach slab represents early-designed bridges. It distinguishes abutment foundation types, not seat and diaphragm abutments, so the same curves appear in seat and diaphragm groups. The horizontal-component definition and the spectral damping of Sa(1.0 s) are not stated.

DS1.Description: Slight damage, the Minor (LS2) state of Shao et al. (2022): rotation of the 10 ft approach slab from backfill settlement, with a slope change of about 1/80 to 1/40; approach settlement exceeds a median capacity of 2.1 in.

DS2.Description: Moderate damage, the Moderate (LS3) state of Shao et al. (2022): rotation of the 10 ft approach slab from backfill settlement, with a slope change of about 1/40 to 1/20; approach settlement exceeds a median capacity of 4.2 in.

DesignSafe PRJ-5910 v1, Sa_1_Fragility Database.csv, data row 35 (spreadsheet row 37), group E123-S1-C0-S, Bearing; source note "T-beam, transverse direction". The curve describes the most-damaged unit of this component type in the bridge (the source analyses record one peak demand per component type), so assign a quantity of one per bridge. Curves for the same component and group from different sources are alternatives, and the database publishes no weights for choosing among them. The component curves do not carry the demand correlation behind the system curves. The component curves and the system curve of the same group (seismic/transportation_network/portfolio/California RC Bridges 2025) are two representations of the same bridge. Apply one or the other to a given bridge, because applying both to the same bridge double-counts its damage; different bridges in one regional assessment may use different representations.

Source study: Cavalcante et al. (2022), a study of typical bridges in northeastern Brazil, including single-span T-beam and slab-deck bridges with seat abutments. Chen et al. (2025) use these curves as a proxy for California single-span bridges. They found no era-specific fragility models for single-span bridges, so the E123 groups apply to bridges of any era. The horizontal-component definition and the spectral damping of Sa(1.0 s) are not stated.

DS1.Description: Slight damage: aesthetic or minor functional damage to the elastomeric bearing pads; bearing deformation exceeds a median capacity of 1 in.

DS2.Description: Moderate damage: significant damage and tearing of the elastomeric bearing pads, which are replaced; bearing deformation exceeds a median capacity of 3 in.

DesignSafe PRJ-5910 v1, Sa_1_Fragility Database.csv, data row 129 (spreadsheet row 131), group E2-S2-C1-D, Approach; source note "Abutment on piles with approach slab (length 30 ft) damage through slope offset". The curve describes the most-damaged unit of this component type in the bridge (the source analyses record one peak demand per component type), so assign a quantity of one per bridge. Curves for the same component and group from different sources are alternatives, and the database publishes no weights for choosing among them. Source study: Shao, Xie, Roblee, and Zhang (2022), a study of approach backfill differential settlement for California bridges. The integrated fragility model of the study takes the mean of the three methods' medians and the square root of the sum of squares (SRSS) of their dispersions. The 2D dynamic method uses 320 motions from a parallel Caltrans project with scale factors of 0.8 to 2.5, whose count and range agree with the Caltrans suite of Mangalathu (2017); the 1D static method works from PGA and the 1D dynamic method from stochastic motions, so neither uses these records. The slight and moderate states are the Minor (LS2) and Moderate (LS3) states of the study; its Observable, Major, and Severe states are not included. In the study, the 10 ft approach slab represents early-designed bridges. It distinguishes abutment foundation types, not seat and diaphragm abutments, so the same curves appear in seat and diaphragm groups. The horizontal-component definition and the spectral damping of Sa(1.0 s) are not stated.

DS1.Description: Slight damage, the Minor (LS2) state of Shao et al. (2022): rotation of the 30 ft approach slab from backfill settlement, with a slope change of about 1/80 to 1/40; approach settlement exceeds a median capacity of 6.4 in.

DS2.Description: Moderate damage, the Moderate (LS3) state of Shao et al. (2022): rotation of the 30 ft approach slab from backfill settlement, with a slope change of about 1/40 to 1/20; approach settlement exceeds a median capacity of 12.7 in.

DesignSafe PRJ-5910 v1, Sa_1_Fragility Database.csv, data row 558 (spreadsheet row 560), group E2-S2-C1-S, Approach; source note "Cantilever abutment on spread footing with approach slab damage through slope offset, with an approach slab length of 30 ft.". The curve describes the most-damaged unit of this component type in the bridge (the source analyses record one peak demand per component type), so assign a quantity of one per bridge. Curves for the same component and group from different sources are alternatives, and the database publishes no weights for choosing among them. The component curves do not carry the demand correlation behind the system curves. The component curves and the system curve of the same group (seismic/transportation_network/portfolio/California RC Bridges 2025) are two representations of the same bridge. Apply one or the other to a given bridge, because applying both to the same bridge double-counts its damage; different bridges in one regional assessment may use different representations.

Source study: Shao, Xie, Roblee, and Zhang (2022), a study of approach backfill differential settlement for California bridges. The integrated fragility model of the study takes the mean of the three methods' medians and the square root of the sum of squares (SRSS) of their dispersions. The 2D dynamic method uses 320 motions from a parallel Caltrans project with scale factors of 0.8 to 2.5, whose count and range agree with the Caltrans suite of Mangalathu (2017); the 1D static method works from PGA and the 1D dynamic method from stochastic motions, so neither uses these records. The slight and moderate states are the Minor (LS2) and Moderate (LS3) states of the study; its Observable, Major, and Severe states are not included. In the study, the 10 ft approach slab represents early-designed bridges. It distinguishes abutment foundation types, not seat and diaphragm abutments, so the same curves appear in seat and diaphragm groups. The horizontal-component definition and the spectral damping of Sa(1.0 s) are not stated.

The source gives N/A for the moderate state, which the database uses to mark a negligible probability of that damage from ground shaking.

DS1.Description: Slight damage, the Minor (LS2) state of Shao et al. (2022): rotation of the 30 ft approach slab from backfill settlement, with a slope change of about 1/80 to 1/40; approach settlement exceeds a median capacity of 6.4 in.

Source study: Shao, Xie, Roblee, and Zhang (2022), a study of approach backfill differential settlement for California bridges. The integrated fragility model of the study takes the mean of the three methods' medians and the square root of the sum of squares (SRSS) of their dispersions. The 2D dynamic method uses 320 motions from a parallel Caltrans project with scale factors of 0.8 to 2.5, whose count and range agree with the Caltrans suite of Mangalathu (2017); the 1D static method works from PGA and the 1D dynamic method from stochastic motions, so neither uses these records. The slight and moderate states are the Minor (LS2) and Moderate (LS3) states of the study; its Observable, Major, and Severe states are not included. In the study, the 10 ft approach slab represents early-designed bridges. It distinguishes abutment foundation types, not seat and diaphragm abutments, so the same curves appear in seat and diaphragm groups. The horizontal-component definition and the spectral damping of Sa(1.0 s) are not stated.

DS1.Description: Slight damage, the Minor (LS2) state of Shao et al. (2022): rotation of the 30 ft approach slab from backfill settlement, with a slope change of about 1/80 to 1/40; approach settlement exceeds a median capacity of 6.4 in.

DS2.Description: Moderate damage, the Moderate (LS3) state of Shao et al. (2022): rotation of the 30 ft approach slab from backfill settlement, with a slope change of about 1/40 to 1/20; approach settlement exceeds a median capacity of 12.7 in.

Source study: Shao, Xie, Roblee, and Zhang (2022), a study of approach backfill differential settlement for California bridges. The integrated fragility model of the study takes the mean of the three methods' medians and the square root of the sum of squares (SRSS) of their dispersions. The 2D dynamic method uses 320 motions from a parallel Caltrans project with scale factors of 0.8 to 2.5, whose count and range agree with the Caltrans suite of Mangalathu (2017); the 1D static method works from PGA and the 1D dynamic method from stochastic motions, so neither uses these records. The slight and moderate states are the Minor (LS2) and Moderate (LS3) states of the study; its Observable, Major, and Severe states are not included. In the study, the 10 ft approach slab represents early-designed bridges. It distinguishes abutment foundation types, not seat and diaphragm abutments, so the same curves appear in seat and diaphragm groups. The horizontal-component definition and the spectral damping of Sa(1.0 s) are not stated.

The source gives N/A for the moderate state, which the database uses to mark a negligible probability of that damage from ground shaking.

Source study: Shao, Xie, Roblee, and Zhang (2022), a study of approach backfill differential settlement for California bridges. The integrated fragility model of the study takes the mean of the three methods' medians and the square root of the sum of squares (SRSS) of their dispersions. The 2D dynamic method uses 320 motions from a parallel Caltrans project with scale factors of 0.8 to 2.5, whose count and range agree with the Caltrans suite of Mangalathu (2017); the 1D static method works from PGA and the 1D dynamic method from stochastic motions, so neither uses these records. The slight and moderate states are the Minor (LS2) and Moderate (LS3) states of the study; its Observable, Major, and Severe states are not included. In the study, the 10 ft approach slab represents early-designed bridges. It distinguishes abutment foundation types, not seat and diaphragm abutments, so the same curves appear in seat and diaphragm groups. The horizontal-component definition and the spectral damping of Sa(1.0 s) are not stated.

The source gives N/A for the moderate state, which the database uses to mark a negligible probability of that damage from ground shaking.

DS1.Description: Slight damage: cracking of the column, repaired by sealing and painting; column curvature ductility exceeds a median capacity of 1 (Era 2).

DS2.Description: Moderate damage: minor spalling of the cover concrete, repaired by epoxy injection and minor concrete removal and patching; column curvature ductility exceeds a median capacity of 5 (Era 2).

DS3.Description: Extensive damage: exposed core and yielding of the transverse reinforcement; major repairs are needed, but the column keeps its function; column curvature ductility exceeds a median capacity of 8 (Era 2).

DS4.Description: Complete damage: longitudinal bar buckling, core crushing, or large drift; the column function is compromised and the column (or the bridge) is replaced; column curvature ductility exceeds a median capacity of 11 (Era 2).

Source study: Shao, Xie, Roblee, and Zhang (2022), a study of approach backfill differential settlement for California bridges. The integrated fragility model of the study takes the mean of the three methods' medians and the square root of the sum of squares (SRSS) of their dispersions. The 2D dynamic method uses 320 motions from a parallel Caltrans project with scale factors of 0.8 to 2.5, whose count and range agree with the Caltrans suite of Mangalathu (2017); the 1D static method works from PGA and the 1D dynamic method from stochastic motions, so neither uses these records. The slight and moderate states are the Minor (LS2) and Moderate (LS3) states of the study; its Observable, Major, and Severe states are not included. In the study, the 10 ft approach slab represents early-designed bridges. It distinguishes abutment foundation types, not seat and diaphragm abutments, so the same curves appear in seat and diaphragm groups. The horizontal-component definition and the spectral damping of Sa(1.0 s) are not stated.

CRCB.E2.S3P.C1.D.Unseating.BoxGirder.Spa.Description: Span unseating fragility for an Era 2 (1971–1990) bridge with three or more spans, single-column bents, and diaphragm abutments. Model attributes: box-girder deck, five modeled spans, multiple frames, in-span hinge, circular columns.
CRCB.E2.S3P.C1.D.Unseating.BoxGirder.Spa.Comments:
DesignSafe PRJ-5910 v1, Sa_1_Fragility Database.csv, data row 316 (spreadsheet row 318), group E2-S3P-C1-D, Unseating; source note "Box-girder, multiple frames, circular columnonly for discontinuous bridges". The curve describes the most-damaged unit of this component type in the bridge (the source analyses record one peak demand per component type), so assign a quantity of one per bridge. Curves for the same component and group from different sources are alternatives, and the database publishes no weights for choosing among them. The component curves do not carry the demand correlation behind the system curves. The component curves and the system curve of the same group (seismic/transportation_network/portfolio/California RC Bridges 2025) are two representations of the same bridge. Apply one or the other to a given bridge, because applying both to the same bridge double-counts its damage; different bridges in one regional assessment may use different representations.

Source study: Mangalathu, Choi, Park, and Jeon (2018), a study of tall, horizontally curved concrete box-girder bridges in California. The analyses use the Baker et al. (2011) PEER transportation suite scaled by a factor of two (320 motions). The study models one configuration: two frames, five spans, single-column bents with circular columns, an in-span hinge, and integral abutments, with three column heights and several deck curvatures. The database does not state which column height and curvature its curves represent. Chen et al. (2025, Table 3) list the study as seat-type; its bridges have integral abutments (Fig. 3 and Conclusions of the study), which is consistent with the placement of its curves in the diaphragm groups. Curves marked Disc (in-span hinge) describe the bearings and the seat at the hinge and apply only to bridges with an intermediate expansion joint. The horizontal-component definition and the spectral damping of Sa(1.0 s) are not stated.

The source defines unseating capacity for extensive and complete only. The slight and moderate limit states are set equal to the extensive limit state so that pelicun can evaluate the model; those two states cannot occur.

DS1.Description: Slight damage: not defined by the source; this state cannot occur (capacity set equal to extensive).

DS2.Description: Moderate damage: not defined by the source; this state cannot occur (capacity set equal to extensive).

DS3.Description: Extensive damage: seat displacement of more than about half the minimum seat width; joint opening exceeds a median capacity of 10 in. (Era 2).

DS4.Description: Complete damage: loss of seat support, with potential unseating of the span; joint opening exceeds a median capacity of 15 in. (Era 2).

Source study: Shao, Xie, Roblee, and Zhang (2022), a study of approach backfill differential settlement for California bridges. The integrated fragility model of the study takes the mean of the three methods' medians and the square root of the sum of squares (SRSS) of their dispersions. The 2D dynamic method uses 320 motions from a parallel Caltrans project with scale factors of 0.8 to 2.5, whose count and range agree with the Caltrans suite of Mangalathu (2017); the 1D static method works from PGA and the 1D dynamic method from stochastic motions, so neither uses these records. The slight and moderate states are the Minor (LS2) and Moderate (LS3) states of the study; its Observable, Major, and Severe states are not included. In the study, the 10 ft approach slab represents early-designed bridges. It distinguishes abutment foundation types, not seat and diaphragm abutments, so the same curves appear in seat and diaphragm groups. The horizontal-component definition and the spectral damping of Sa(1.0 s) are not stated.

The source gives N/A for the moderate state, which the database uses to mark a negligible probability of that damage from ground shaking.

DS1.Description: Slight damage, the Minor (LS2) state of Shao et al. (2022): rotation of the 30 ft approach slab from backfill settlement, with a slope change of about 1/80 to 1/40; approach settlement exceeds a median capacity of 6.4 in.

CRCB.E2.S3P.C2P.D.AbTran.BoxGirder.TCB.S.Description: Transverse abutment fragility for an Era 2 (1971–1990) bridge with three or more spans, multi-column bents, and diaphragm abutments. Model attributes: box-girder deck, two-column bents, three modeled spans, oblong columns.
CRCB.E2.S3P.C2P.D.AbTran.BoxGirder.TCB.S.Comments:
DesignSafe PRJ-5910 v1, Sa_1_Fragility Database.csv, data row 348 (spreadsheet row 350), group E2-S3P-C2P-D, AbTran; source note "Box-girder, oblong column". The curve describes the most-damaged unit of this component type in the bridge (the source analyses record one peak demand per component type), so assign a quantity of one per bridge. Curves for the same component and group from different sources are alternatives, and the database publishes no weights for choosing among them. The component curves do not carry the demand correlation behind the system curves. The component curves and the system curve of the same group (seismic/transportation_network/portfolio/California RC Bridges 2025) are two representations of the same bridge. Apply one or the other to a given bridge, because applying both to the same bridge double-counts its damage; different bridges in one regional assessment may use different representations.

Source study: Jeon, Mangalathu, and Lee (2019), a study of California concrete box-girder bridges with flared two-column bents. The analyses use the Baker et al. (2011) PEER transportation suite scaled by a factor of two (320 motions). The authors state that the curves are valid only for the selected bridge classes: straight three-span Era 2 bridges with two-column bents. Flared columns: Flr1 is a one-way flared column with a 102 mm (4 in.) gap between the flare and the superstructure (BRIDGE-G of the study), Flr1T a one-way flared column along the transverse direction without a gap (BRIDGE-F1), and Flr2 a two-way flared column (BRIDGE-F2). The horizontal-component definition and the spectral damping of Sa(1.0 s) are not stated.

Source study: Shao, Xie, Roblee, and Zhang (2022), a study of approach backfill differential settlement for California bridges. The integrated fragility model of the study takes the mean of the three methods' medians and the square root of the sum of squares (SRSS) of their dispersions. The 2D dynamic method uses 320 motions from a parallel Caltrans project with scale factors of 0.8 to 2.5, whose count and range agree with the Caltrans suite of Mangalathu (2017); the 1D static method works from PGA and the 1D dynamic method from stochastic motions, so neither uses these records. The slight and moderate states are the Minor (LS2) and Moderate (LS3) states of the study; its Observable, Major, and Severe states are not included. In the study, the 10 ft approach slab represents early-designed bridges. It distinguishes abutment foundation types, not seat and diaphragm abutments, so the same curves appear in seat and diaphragm groups. The horizontal-component definition and the spectral damping of Sa(1.0 s) are not stated.

Source study: Mangalathu (2017), a doctoral thesis that groups California box-girder bridges into classes by design era, span count, bent type, abutment type, and column shape, and derives component and system fragilities for each class from nonlinear time-history analyses. The fragility analyses use 320 scaled motions from 228 records of a Caltrans NGA-West2 suite listed in thesis Appendix A. Sa(1.0 s) is the RotD50 spectral acceleration at 5% damping: for 317 of the 320 motions, the Appendix A value equals the NGA-West2 RotD50 value times the tabulated scale factor.

The parameters are identical to those of CRCB.E2.S3P.C2P.D.Column.BoxGirder.MCB.Obl.M17; the duplication is in the source.

DS1.Description: Slight damage: cracking of the column, repaired by sealing and painting; column curvature ductility exceeds a median capacity of 1 (Era 2).

DS2.Description: Moderate damage: minor spalling of the cover concrete, repaired by epoxy injection and minor concrete removal and patching; column curvature ductility exceeds a median capacity of 5 (Era 2).

DS3.Description: Extensive damage: exposed core and yielding of the transverse reinforcement; major repairs are needed, but the column keeps its function; column curvature ductility exceeds a median capacity of 8 (Era 2).

DS4.Description: Complete damage: longitudinal bar buckling, core crushing, or large drift; the column function is compromised and the column (or the bridge) is replaced; column curvature ductility exceeds a median capacity of 11 (Era 2).

Source study: Shao, Xie, Roblee, and Zhang (2022), a study of approach backfill differential settlement for California bridges. The integrated fragility model of the study takes the mean of the three methods' medians and the square root of the sum of squares (SRSS) of their dispersions. The 2D dynamic method uses 320 motions from a parallel Caltrans project with scale factors of 0.8 to 2.5, whose count and range agree with the Caltrans suite of Mangalathu (2017); the 1D static method works from PGA and the 1D dynamic method from stochastic motions, so neither uses these records. The slight and moderate states are the Minor (LS2) and Moderate (LS3) states of the study; its Observable, Major, and Severe states are not included. In the study, the 10 ft approach slab represents early-designed bridges. It distinguishes abutment foundation types, not seat and diaphragm abutments, so the same curves appear in seat and diaphragm groups. The horizontal-component definition and the spectral damping of Sa(1.0 s) are not stated.

The source gives N/A for the moderate state, which the database uses to mark a negligible probability of that damage from ground shaking.

The curve describes the most-damaged unit of this component type in the bridge (the source analyses record one peak demand per component type), so assign a quantity of one per bridge. Source study: Shao, Xie, Roblee, and Zhang (2022), a study of approach backfill differential settlement for California bridges. The integrated fragility model of the study takes the mean of the three methods' medians and the square root of the sum of squares (SRSS) of their dispersions. The 2D dynamic method uses 320 motions from a parallel Caltrans project with scale factors of 0.8 to 2.5, whose count and range agree with the Caltrans suite of Mangalathu (2017); the 1D static method works from PGA and the 1D dynamic method from stochastic motions, so neither uses these records. The slight and moderate states are the Minor (LS2) and Moderate (LS3) states of the study; its Observable, Major, and Severe states are not included. In the study, the 10 ft approach slab represents early-designed bridges. It distinguishes abutment foundation types, not seat and diaphragm abutments, so the same curves appear in seat and diaphragm groups. The horizontal-component definition and the spectral damping of Sa(1.0 s) are not stated.

CRCB.E2.S3P.C2P.S.Bearing.BoxGirder.MCB..Comments:
DesignSafe PRJ-5910 v1, Sa_1_Fragility Database.csv, data row 881 (spreadsheet row 883), group E2-S3P-C2P-S, Bearing; source note "Box-girder, circular column". The curve describes the most-damaged unit of this component type in the bridge (the source analyses record one peak demand per component type), so assign a quantity of one per bridge. Curves for the same component and group from different sources are alternatives, and the database publishes no weights for choosing among them. Source study: Mangalathu (2017), a doctoral thesis that groups California box-girder bridges into classes by design era, span count, bent type, abutment type, and column shape, and derives component and system fragilities for each class from nonlinear time-history analyses. Sa(1.0 s) is the RotD50 spectral acceleration at 5% damping: for 317 of the 320 motions, the Appendix A value equals the NGA-West2 RotD50 value times the tabulated scale factor.

Flared columns: Flr1 is a one-way flared column with a 102 mm (4 in.) gap between the flare and the superstructure (BRIDGE-G of the study), Flr1T a one-way flared column along the transverse direction without a gap (BRIDGE-F1), and Flr2 a two-way flared column (BRIDGE-F2). The horizontal-component definition and the spectral damping of Sa(1.0 s) are not stated.

The published parameters equal those of CRCB.E2.S3P.C2P.S.Bearing.BoxGirder.TCB.Span3.Obl.JML19 at the two decimals of the source; Jeon, Mangalathu, and Lee (2019, Tables 4 and 5) give values for the two configurations that differ by less than that rounding.

Source study: Shao, Xie, Roblee, and Zhang (2022), a study of approach backfill differential settlement for California bridges. The integrated fragility model of the study takes the mean of the three methods' medians and the square root of the sum of squares (SRSS) of their dispersions. The 2D dynamic method uses 320 motions from a parallel Caltrans project with scale factors of 0.8 to 2.5, whose count and range agree with the Caltrans suite of Mangalathu (2017); the 1D static method works from PGA and the 1D dynamic method from stochastic motions, so neither uses these records. The slight and moderate states are the Minor (LS2) and Moderate (LS3) states of the study; its Observable, Major, and Severe states are not included. In the study, the 10 ft approach slab represents early-designed bridges. It distinguishes abutment foundation types, not seat and diaphragm abutments, so the same curves appear in seat and diaphragm groups. The horizontal-component definition and the spectral damping of Sa(1.0 s) are not stated.

In the study, the 10 ft approach slab represents early-designed bridges. It distinguishes abutment foundation types, not seat and diaphragm abutments, so the same curves appear in seat and diaphragm groups. The horizontal-component definition and the spectral damping of Sa(1.0 s) are not stated.

Source study: Shao, Xie, Roblee, and Zhang (2022), a study of approach backfill differential settlement for California bridges. The integrated fragility model of the study takes the mean of the three methods' medians and the square root of the sum of squares (SRSS) of their dispersions. The 2D dynamic method uses 320 motions from a parallel Caltrans project with scale factors of 0.8 to 2.5, whose count and range agree with the Caltrans suite of Mangalathu (2017); the 1D static method works from PGA and the 1D dynamic method from stochastic motions, so neither uses these records. The slight and moderate states are the Minor (LS2) and Moderate (LS3) states of the study; its Observable, Major, and Severe states are not included. In the study, the 10 ft approach slab represents early-designed bridges. It distinguishes abutment foundation types, not seat and diaphragm abutments, so the same curves appear in seat and diaphragm groups. The horizontal-component definition and the spectral damping of Sa(1.0 s) are not stated.

Source study: Shao, Xie, Roblee, and Zhang (2022), a study of approach backfill differential settlement for California bridges. The integrated fragility model of the study takes the mean of the three methods' medians and the square root of the sum of squares (SRSS) of their dispersions. The 2D dynamic method uses 320 motions from a parallel Caltrans project with scale factors of 0.8 to 2.5, whose count and range agree with the Caltrans suite of Mangalathu (2017); the 1D static method works from PGA and the 1D dynamic method from stochastic motions, so neither uses these records. The slight and moderate states are the Minor (LS2) and Moderate (LS3) states of the study; its Observable, Major, and Severe states are not included. In the study, the 10 ft approach slab represents early-designed bridges. It distinguishes abutment foundation types, not seat and diaphragm abutments, so the same curves appear in seat and diaphragm groups. The horizontal-component definition and the spectral damping of Sa(1.0 s) are not stated.

The source gives N/A for the moderate state, which the database uses to mark a negligible probability of that damage from ground shaking.

DS1.Description: Slight damage, the Minor (LS2) state of Shao et al. (2022): rotation of the 30 ft approach slab from backfill settlement, with a slope change of about 1/80 to 1/40; approach settlement exceeds a median capacity of 6.4 in.

DesignSafe PRJ-5910 v1, Sa_1_Fragility Database.csv, data row 699 (spreadsheet row 701), group E3-S2-C2P-S, Approach; source note "Regular-height abutment on spread footing with approach slab damage through step offset.". The curve describes the most-damaged unit of this component type in the bridge (the source analyses record one peak demand per component type), so assign a quantity of one per bridge. Curves for the same component and group from different sources are alternatives, and the database publishes no weights for choosing among them. The component curves do not carry the demand correlation behind the system curves. The component curves and the system curve of the same group (seismic/transportation_network/portfolio/California RC Bridges 2025) are two representations of the same bridge. Apply one or the other to a given bridge, because applying both to the same bridge double-counts its damage; different bridges in one regional assessment may use different representations.

Source study: Shao, Xie, Roblee, and Zhang (2022), a study of approach backfill differential settlement for California bridges. The integrated fragility model of the study takes the mean of the three methods' medians and the square root of the sum of squares (SRSS) of their dispersions. The 2D dynamic method uses 320 motions from a parallel Caltrans project with scale factors of 0.8 to 2.5, whose count and range agree with the Caltrans suite of Mangalathu (2017); the 1D static method works from PGA and the 1D dynamic method from stochastic motions, so neither uses these records. The slight and moderate states are the Minor (LS2) and Moderate (LS3) states of the study; its Observable, Major, and Severe states are not included. In the study, the 10 ft approach slab represents early-designed bridges. It distinguishes abutment foundation types, not seat and diaphragm abutments, so the same curves appear in seat and diaphragm groups. The horizontal-component definition and the spectral damping of Sa(1.0 s) are not stated.

DS1.Description: Slight damage, the Minor (LS2) state of Shao et al. (2022): step offset between the approach pavement and the abutment from backfill settlement; approach settlement exceeds a median capacity of 1.4 in.

DS2.Description: Moderate damage, the Moderate (LS3) state of Shao et al. (2022): step offset between the approach pavement and the abutment from backfill settlement; approach settlement exceeds a median capacity of 2.5 in.

The curve describes the most-damaged unit of this component type in the bridge (the source analyses record one peak demand per component type), so assign a quantity of one per bridge. Curves for the same component and group from different sources are alternatives, and the database publishes no weights for choosing among them. The component curves do not carry the demand correlation behind the system curves. The component curves and the system curve of the same group (seismic/transportation_network/portfolio/California RC Bridges 2025) are two representations of the same bridge. Source study: Mangalathu (2017), a doctoral thesis that groups California box-girder bridges into classes by design era, span count, bent type, abutment type, and column shape, and derives component and system fragilities for each class from nonlinear time-history analyses. DS1.Description: Slight damage: aesthetic or minor functional damage to the elastomeric bearing pads; bearing deformation exceeds a median capacity of 1 in.

DS2.Description: Moderate damage: significant damage and tearing of the elastomeric bearing pads, which are replaced; bearing deformation exceeds a median capacity of 4 in.

Source study: Shao, Xie, Roblee, and Zhang (2022), a study of approach backfill differential settlement for California bridges. The integrated fragility model of the study takes the mean of the three methods' medians and the square root of the sum of squares (SRSS) of their dispersions. The 2D dynamic method uses 320 motions from a parallel Caltrans project with scale factors of 0.8 to 2.5, whose count and range agree with the Caltrans suite of Mangalathu (2017); the 1D static method works from PGA and the 1D dynamic method from stochastic motions, so neither uses these records. In the study, the 10 ft approach slab represents early-designed bridges. It distinguishes abutment foundation types, not seat and diaphragm abutments, so the same curves appear in seat and diaphragm groups. The horizontal-component definition and the spectral damping of Sa(1.0 s) are not stated.

Source study: Shao, Xie, Roblee, and Zhang (2022), a study of approach backfill differential settlement for California bridges. The integrated fragility model of the study takes the mean of the three methods' medians and the square root of the sum of squares (SRSS) of their dispersions. The 2D dynamic method uses 320 motions from a parallel Caltrans project with scale factors of 0.8 to 2.5, whose count and range agree with the Caltrans suite of Mangalathu (2017); the 1D static method works from PGA and the 1D dynamic method from stochastic motions, so neither uses these records. The slight and moderate states are the Minor (LS2) and Moderate (LS3) states of the study; its Observable, Major, and Severe states are not included. In the study, the 10 ft approach slab represents early-designed bridges. It distinguishes abutment foundation types, not seat and diaphragm abutments, so the same curves appear in seat and diaphragm groups. The horizontal-component definition and the spectral damping of Sa(1.0 s) are not stated.

DesignSafe PRJ-5910 v1, Sa_1_Fragility Database.csv, data row 936 (spreadsheet row 938), group E3-S3P-C1-S, DeckMax; source note "Box-girder, circular column". The curve describes the most-damaged unit of this component type in the bridge (the source analyses record one peak demand per component type), so assign a quantity of one per bridge. Curves for the same component and group from different sources are alternatives, and the database publishes no weights for choosing among them. The component curves do not carry the demand correlation behind the system curves. The component curves and the system curve of the same group (seismic/transportation_network/portfolio/California RC Bridges 2025) are two representations of the same bridge. Apply one or the other to a given bridge, because applying both to the same bridge double-counts its damage; different bridges in one regional assessment may use different representations.

Source study: Mangalathu (2017), a doctoral thesis that groups California box-girder bridges into classes by design era, span count, bent type, abutment type, and column shape, and derives component and system fragilities for each class from nonlinear time-history analyses. The fragility analyses use 320 scaled motions from 228 records of a Caltrans NGA-West2 suite listed in thesis Appendix A. Sa(1.0 s) is the RotD50 spectral acceleration at 5% damping: for 317 of the 320 motions, the Appendix A value equals the NGA-West2 RotD50 value times the tabulated scale factor.

DS1.Description: Slight damage: aesthetic or minor functional damage associated with large deck displacement, typically repaired by injecting epoxy into cracks; maximum deck displacement exceeds a median capacity of 4 in.

DS2.Description: Moderate damage: major functional damage associated with large deck displacement; maximum deck displacement exceeds a median capacity of 12 in.

Source study: Shao, Xie, Roblee, and Zhang (2022), a study of approach backfill differential settlement for California bridges. The integrated fragility model of the study takes the mean of the three methods' medians and the square root of the sum of squares (SRSS) of their dispersions. The 2D dynamic method uses 320 motions from a parallel Caltrans project with scale factors of 0.8 to 2.5, whose count and range agree with the Caltrans suite of Mangalathu (2017); the 1D static method works from PGA and the 1D dynamic method from stochastic motions, so neither uses these records. The slight and moderate states are the Minor (LS2) and Moderate (LS3) states of the study; its Observable, Major, and Severe states are not included. In the study, the 10 ft approach slab represents early-designed bridges. It distinguishes abutment foundation types, not seat and diaphragm abutments, so the same curves appear in seat and diaphragm groups. The horizontal-component definition and the spectral damping of Sa(1.0 s) are not stated.

Source study: Shao, Xie, Roblee, and Zhang (2022), a study of approach backfill differential settlement for California bridges. The integrated fragility model of the study takes the mean of the three methods' medians and the square root of the sum of squares (SRSS) of their dispersions. The 2D dynamic method uses 320 motions from a parallel Caltrans project with scale factors of 0.8 to 2.5, whose count and range agree with the Caltrans suite of Mangalathu (2017); the 1D static method works from PGA and the 1D dynamic method from stochastic motions, so neither uses these records. The slight and moderate states are the Minor (LS2) and Moderate (LS3) states of the study; its Observable, Major, and Severe states are not included. In the study, the 10 ft approach slab represents early-designed bridges. It distinguishes abutment foundation types, not seat and diaphragm abutments, so the same curves appear in seat and diaphragm groups. The horizontal-component definition and the spectral damping of Sa(1.0 s) are not stated.

The source gives N/A for the moderate state, which the database uses to mark a negligible probability of that damage from ground shaking.

DS1.Description: Slight damage, the Minor (LS2) state of Shao et al. (2022): rotation of the 30 ft approach slab from backfill settlement, with a slope change of about 1/80 to 1/40; approach settlement exceeds a median capacity of 6.4 in.

CRCB.E3.S3P.C2P.S.Unseating.BoxGirder.TC.Description: Span unseating fragility for an Era 3 (post-1991) bridge with three or more spans, multi-column bents, and seat abutments. Model attributes: box-girder deck, two-column bents, oblong columns.
CRCB.E3.S3P.C2P.S.Unseating.BoxGirder.TC.Comments:
DesignSafe PRJ-5910 v1, Sa_1_Fragility Database.csv, data row 966 (spreadsheet row 968), group E3-S3P-C2P-S, Unseating; source note "Box-girder, oblong column". The curve describes the most-damaged unit of this component type in the bridge (the source analyses record one peak demand per component type), so assign a quantity of one per bridge. Curves for the same component and group from different sources are alternatives, and the database publishes no weights for choosing among them. The component curves do not carry the demand correlation behind the system curves. The component curves and the system curve of the same group (seismic/transportation_network/portfolio/California RC Bridges 2025) are two representations of the same bridge. Apply one or the other to a given bridge, because applying both to the same bridge double-counts its damage; different bridges in one regional assessment may use different representations.

Source study: Mangalathu (2017), a doctoral thesis that groups California box-girder bridges into classes by design era, span count, bent type, abutment type, and column shape, and derives component and system fragilities for each class from nonlinear time-history analyses. The fragility analyses use 320 scaled motions from 228 records of a Caltrans NGA-West2 suite listed in thesis Appendix A. Sa(1.0 s) is the RotD50 spectral acceleration at 5% damping: for 317 of the 320 motions, the Appendix A value equals the NGA-West2 RotD50 value times the tabulated scale factor.

The curve equals the Era 2 curve of the same class, as in Mangalathu (2017) Appendix C.

DS1.Description: Slight damage: joint opening about equal to the expansion-joint gap; onset of pounding damage; joint opening exceeds a median capacity of 1 in. (Era 2 value).

DS2.Description: Moderate damage: significant pounding at the seat joint; joint opening exceeds a median capacity of 4.5 in. (Era 2 value).

DS3.Description: Extensive damage: seat displacement of more than about half the minimum seat width; joint opening exceeds a median capacity of 10 in. (Era 2 value).

DS4.Description: Complete damage: loss of seat support, with potential unseating of the span; joint opening exceeds a median capacity of 15 in. (Era 2 value).
